verdicts.claim: simd_float4x4 is NOT Codable. Its documented conformances are exactly: BitwiseCopyable, Copyable, CustomDebugStringConvertible, Equatable, Escapable, Sendable. A wrapper is required for JSON (e.g. encode columns.0...columns.3 as [Float] of 16 values, column-major) or store poses in a binary blob. simd_float3x3 (ARCamera.intrinsics) likewise needs a wrapper.
verdicts.reasoning: I fetched the doc JSON for simd_float4x4. Its 'Conforms To' list is exactly BitwiseCopyable, Copyable, CustomDebugStringConvertible, Equatable, Escapable, Sendable. The simd_float3x3 doc JSON (https://developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/documentation/simd/simd_float3x3.json) lists the same six. The Swift stdlib makes the generic SIMD2/3/4 vector types Codable, but the matrix types are imported C structs and get no Codable conformance. So a wrapper, such as 16 column-major Floats or a binary blob, is required.

verdicts.claim: Long-running processing cannot be continued in the background on iOS 18. BGContinuedProcessingTask / BGContinuedProcessingTaskRequest (start in foreground, continue in background with a Live Activity) are iOS 26.0+ only. On iOS 18 the options are: (a) beginBackgroundTask(withName:expirationHandler:) which gives 'a limited amount of time' (community: ~30 s) and (b) BGProcessingTask which 'run[s] only when the device is idle' and 'The system terminates any background processing tasks running when the user starts using the device' (needs UIBackgroundModes=processing + BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers, registration must complete before applicationDidFinishLaunching ends). Therefore mesh/photogrammetry processing must run while the app is foregrounded; keep the screen awake with UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled = true.
verdicts.reasoning: The doc JSON for both BGContinuedProcessingTaskRequest and BGContinuedProcessingTask gives introducedAt iOS 26.0, iPadOS 26.0 and Mac Catalyst 26.0. The request must be submitted from the foreground in response to a person's action. On the Live Activity: 'The system displays the progress of this task in a Live Activity', and the app reports progress through ProgressReporting. The app does not build its own ActivityKit Live Activity. The BGProcessingTask doc (iOS 13.0+) contains both quoted sentences verbatim. The ~30 s figure for beginBackgroundTask comes from the community, not Apple docs, and the claim labels it that way. The conclusion holds on the iOS 18 test device. On iOS 26 devices, the continued task could be an optional path behind an availability check.

verdicts.claim: Swift 6 language mode is opt-in via SWIFT_VERSION=6 (-swift-version 6). XcodeGen's base setting preset hardcodes SWIFT_VERSION: '5.0' for every generated project, so a project.yml that does not override it compiles in Swift 5 mode with minimal concurrency checking: Sendable/actor-isolation problems are at most warnings and will not fail the CI build. Xcode 26 changes only affect NEW Xcode templates (Default Actor Isolation = MainActor); XcodeGen projects get the 'existing project' defaults (SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION unset = nonisolated, SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY unset = NO).
verdicts.correction: Two parts are right: XcodeGen's SettingPresets/base.yml does hardcode SWIFT_VERSION: '5.0', and Swift 5 mode uses minimal strict-concurrency checking by default. The wrong part is 'actor-isolation problems are at most warnings'. In minimal mode, actor-isolation checking still runs wherever code has adopted concurrency, and those violations are hard errors even in Swift 5 mode. Examples: calling a @MainActor-isolated function or property from a synchronous nonisolated context, or calling an async function without await. They will fail the CI build. Only Sendable diagnostics are mostly suppressed or warnings in minimal mode. Also, this repo's ios/project.yml does override the preset, with SWIFT_VERSION: "5.9" in the target's base settings. That is still Swift 5 mode, so the rest of the conclusion applies.
verdicts.reasoning: I confirmed base.yml line 50 reads SWIFT_VERSION: '5.0' (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen/master/SettingPresets/base.yml). The swift.org migration guide describes minimal checking this way: it 'enforces Sendable constraints only where it has been explicitly adopted and performs actor-isolation checking wherever code has adopted concurrency'. Isolation violations on explicitly isolated declarations have been errors in Swift 5 mode since Swift 5.5. The Xcode 26 point is plausible: new templates set default MainActor isolation and Approachable Concurrency, and XcodeGen does not emit those settings. I could not fetch a primary Xcode release-notes page for it, so I left that part unverified.

They match well-known Apple free-provisioning limits (3 apps, 7-day profiles, 10 App IDs per 7 days), and I found no evidence against them.

BGContinuedProcessingTask / BGContinuedProcessingTaskRequest (start in foreground, continue in background with a Live Activity) are iOS 26.0+ only. verdicts.reasoning: Apple doc JSON shows BGContinuedProcessingTaskRequest as introducedAt iOS 26.0, and it also quotes BGProcessingTask's idle-only and terminate-on-use text word for word. Quinn (Apple DTS) writes 'On current systems you can expect about 30 seconds' for UIApplication background tasks, and says not to build logic on backgroundTimeRemaining. The finding is stronger than the claim for GPU work: iOS refuses GPU command submission from the background ('Insufficient Permission (to submit GPU work from background)'). verdicts.claim: Swift 6 language mode is opt-in via SWIFT_VERSION=6 (-swift-version 6). XcodeGen's base setting preset hardcodes SWIFT_VERSION: '5.0' for every generated project, so a project.yml that does not override it compiles in Swift 5 mode with minimal concurrency checking: Sendable/actor-isolation problems are at most warnings and will not fail the CI build. Xcode 26 changes only affect NEW Xcode templates (Default Actor Isolation = MainActor); XcodeGen projects get the 'existing project' defaults (SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION unset = nonisolated, SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY unset = NO).
verdicts.correction: Most of the claim holds. XcodeGen master SettingPresets/base.yml still says SWIFT_VERSION: '5.0' (this project overrides it with '5.9' anyway), and Swift 5 mode defaults to minimal checking. The wrong part is 'at most warnings and will not fail the CI build'. Minimal checking only downgrades missing Sendable conformances and missing global-actor annotations to warnings. Core actor-isolation rules have been hard errors since Swift 5.5 in every language mode. Examples: touching another actor's state synchronously ('actor-isolated property can only be referenced on self'), cross-actor property mutation, a missing await on an async or cross-actor call, and a synchronous call into an actor-isolated method from outside. These fail the build in Swift 5.9 mode too. Only some diagnostics are marked 'this is an error in the Swift 6 language mode' and stay warnings in Swift 5 mode. Module code should still be written isolation-correct.
verdicts.reasoning: I fetched raw.githubusercontent.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen/master/SettingPresets/base.yml, and it ends with SWIFT_VERSION: '5.0'. SE-0337 defines minimal checking as 'Missing Sendable conformances or global-actor annotations are diagnosed as warnings'. That covers only a subset of concurrency diagnostics. SE-0306 (implemented in Swift 5.5) shows 'error: actor-isolated property ... can only be referenced on self' and 'error: cross-actor property mutations are not permitted', and these apply in Swift 5 mode. I found nothing contradicting the Xcode 26 point that only new templates get the new defaults, but I did not check it against an Xcode 26 build log.

Independent sources agree on 3 apps at once, 7-day expiry and 10 App IDs per 7 days: an Apple forum thread 'Limits on App IDs - 10 every 7 days' (thread 675347), SideStore issue #68 and several 2026 sideloading guides. open_question_answers.question: (a) PhotogrammetrySession.Configuration / limits: is there a runtime-readable max input image count on iOS, and what do people report for A15 6 GB devices?
open_question_answers.answer: Yes. `PhotogrammetrySession.limits` is a `static let` of type `PhotogrammetrySession.Limits` (iOS 17+/macOS 14+), described as 'device-specific constant hardware limits'. It exposes `maximumNumberOfInputImages: Int` and `maximumInputImageDimension: Int`. Images over either limit are ignored, and the session reports an .invalidSample-style error for them. There is also an instance property `ObjectCaptureSession.maximumNumberOfInputImages` (@MainActor var, iOS 17+). Capture stops when that limit is reached unless `Configuration.isOverCaptureEnabled` is true. PhotogrammetrySession.Configuration itself (iOS 17+) has no image-count field. I found no reliable published number for A15 6 GB devices. One secondary source cites about 1000 images, but I could not reach the underlying page to confirm it. Read the value at runtime and log it on the test device rather than hardcoding a number.

open_question_answers.question: (b) Can a free-team Sideloadly provisioning profile carry com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit, and is that entitlement available to free accounts at all?
open_question_answers.answer: Apple does make it available to free teams in practice. An Xcode Personal Team build keeps it, and AltStore 2.2 beta and later request the INCREASED_MEMORY_LIMIT bundle-ID capability for free accounts too. SideStore 0.7.0 drops it on free accounts (bug #1616, September 2026). Apple's supported-capabilities table for iOS does not list 'Increased Memory Limit' as its own row, only 'Increased Debugging Memory Limit' and 'Extended Virtual Addressing', both marked for free accounts. I found no evidence either way that Sideloadly enables the capability on the App ID; its FAQ was unreachable. The entitlement only works if the signer enables the capability on the App ID and it ends up in the profile. Test it on the device: sign, then check the embedded.mobileprovision Entitlements and compare os_proc_available_memory with and without it. Apple also warns that the higher limit is only granted on some devices.

open_question_answers.question: (c) Community-reported jetsam memory limit for 6 GB iPhones (13 Pro / 13 Pro Max) on iOS 17/18.
open_question_answers.answer: I found no authoritative per-model figure for 6 GB iPhones on iOS 17/18. Related data points: a 4 GB iPhone 13 on iOS 15.3.1 reported about 2.2 to 2.3 GB from os_proc_available_memory with the increased-memory-limit entitlement (Apple forums 702400). 4 GB iPhone 12 jetsam logs show 'ActiveHard 2098 MB' (forums 688973). The SideStore report mentions roughly 3.3 GB without and about 6 GB with the entitlement, but on an unspecified device, likely one with more RAM. Folklore for 6 GB iPhones is about 2.8 to 3.0 GB by default (around half of RAM), but I could not confirm it. Plan the Object Capture and mesh pipeline for a budget of about 2.5 GB. Log os_proc_available_memory at launch and before reconstruction on the iPhone 13 Pro Max to get the real number.

open_question_answers.question: (a) Free Apple ID device limit per 7 days
open_question_answers.answer: Apple does not document it. Free-team device registrations and provisioning profiles expire after 7 days, and the forums give no specific number (some guess it mirrors the 100-per-year paid limit, but nothing confirms that). The documented, binding limits are 3 active sideloaded apps per device and 10 App IDs per rolling 7 days per Apple ID. Two devices (the 13 Pro Max plus a later iOS 26 phone) on one free Apple ID is routine and far below any reported limit, but each device install of the same bundle ID does not need a new App ID.

open_question_answers.question: (b) Does iOS 26 change any of these (BGContinuedProcessingTask available; SceneKit deprecation affecting runtime or not)
open_question_answers.answer: BGContinuedProcessingTaskRequest exists only on iOS 26.0+, so it needs an #available(iOS 26, *) path. It must be submitted from the foreground in response to a user action. Background GPU (the .gpu resource plus the com.apple.developer.background-tasks.continued-processing.gpu entitlement) is supported only on M3-or-newer iPads, not on any iPhone, per Apple DTS; check BGTaskScheduler.supportedResources at runtime. A free Apple ID personal team also probably cannot sign that entitlement. On an iPhone, continued processing would therefore be CPU-only. SceneKit, SCNView and ARSCNView are marked deprecatedAt 26.0 in Apple's docs ('SceneKit is deprecated, use RealityKit instead'). That is a compile-time deprecation. The code still links and runs on iOS 18 and 26. At worst it adds warnings, which do not fail the CI build, and with an iOS 18.0 deployment target they probably do not fire. New code should prefer RealityKit.

open_question_answers.question: ARKit depth resolution (256x192) and the 1920x1440 default video format are community/WWDC facts, not present in the doc JSON; confirm from ARCamera.imageResolution and CVPixelBufferGetWidth(depthMap) on device.
open_question_answers.answer: Not settled by this pass. No verifier found an Apple doc page that states either number, so code must not hardcode them: read ARCamera.imageResolution and the depthMap pixel buffer width and height at runtime, derive the intrinsics scale from their ratio, and log both on the test device.
